candidates.title: Seal at leaf zero accepts an arbitrary, unverified agreed-state proof (Dave sealLeafMatch / sealInnerMatchAndCreateInnerTournament and the recipe's validate_seal_response)
candidates.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 prt/contracts (Match.sealDivergence -> _requireAgreeState, reached from Tournament.sealLeafMatch and Tournament.sealInnerMatchAndCreateInnerTournament); PRT referee model in doc/recipes (prt.lua validate_seal_response)
candidates.role: Referee model, as the deployed referee (Dave); Referee model (doc/recipes/prt.lua)
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/prt/contracts/src/tournament/libs/Match.sol _requireAgreeState (~l.289-303: 'if (divergencePosition == 0) { require(agreeState.eq(args.initialHash)); return; }', agreeStateProof never looked at), callers Tournament.sol sealLeafMatch (~528-574) and sealInnerMatchAndCreateInnerTournament (~677-732); doc/recipes/prt.lua validate_seal_response (310-339, 'if leaf_index ~= 0 then ... else agreed_state_hash = tournament.initial_state_hash end': response.agreed_state_hash_proof is ignored at leaf zero); manual doc/README.md 'The tournament' ('At leaf zero, the agreed state is the tournament's initial state hash, which the referee already knows').
candidates.description: When a bisection converges on leaf zero the referee needs no agreed-state proof: the agreed state is the tournament's initial hash. Both referees then accept the seal whatever the proof argument holds. Dave's _requireAgreeState returns after comparing agreeState with initialHash and never reads agreeStateProof, so a seal transaction with a proof array of any length and content succeeds (for a non-zero position the same function demands exactly `height` siblings that roll up to the revealing commitment). The recipe's validate_seal_response likewise never looks at response.agreed_state_hash_proof when leaf_index == 0. This is the same class as R1-R3-3 (the model accepts superfluous logs in a state-transition proof) at another site, and here the deployed referee shows it too. The superfluous data does not change the sealed divergence (agree state, position, contested states), so no result is affected. In Dave the seal refund is metered with meteredBytes = 0, so padding does not raise the refund. A related generalisation in the model: the transport decodes every response with cartesi.fromjson under schemas that neither require the declared fields nor reject unknown ones, so every validator accepts responses with extra fields.
candidates.trigger: Any party that seals a match whose first divergent leaf is leaf 0 (it can post the seal with a junk or oversized proof). Reaching leaf 0 only needs a claim that lies about the first sampled state.
candidates.reachability: Reachable in every tournament, at both levels: a dishonest claim whose first leaf differs from the honest one makes the bisection end at position 0, and the first-step dispute of any uarch tournament (uarch leaf 0) is the common case (the manual's own forger and tamperer matches end at 'state 0').
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: no; nothing in the out-of-scope list is needed (the trigger is a claimant's seal move, 'dishonest claimants (any number, any logs, any proofs, any timing)'). 2. Role: Dave is the 'Referee model, as the deployed referee' and prt.lua the 'Referee model' (AUDIT.md table); section 3: 'A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it.' 3. High/Medium cases: Medium, 'A referee verifier that accepts trailing data that does not affect its result (R3). A support verifier that does so is Low.' R3: 'Conditions on the log are validity conditions. A log that fails one must be rejected. Examples are wrong order, wrong address, wrong size, duplicate, missing, or trailing data'; section 4: 'A verifier must assume that every count, index, address, size, and hash it receives was chosen to fool it.' The proof argument at leaf zero is data that the acceptance does not depend on. Alternative reading: Low, if that Medium case is read as covering only the verifiers of transition logs and not the computation-hash proof checks of the tournament (then it 'violates no rule or obligation of this model'). The campaign confirmed the sibling R1-R3-3 as Medium / Low on the same two readings. 4. Critical: no; the accepted seal derives the same divergence and no after-hash or winner changes. 5. Otherwise Low.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (Low under the narrower reading of the trailing-data case)
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not threaten the goal of section 1: the sealed agree state is the on-chain initial hash and the contested leaves come from the bisection. It breaks the discipline of R3 that superfluous or malformed proof data is a validity failure, and it makes the model and Dave accept two different seal moves for the same position, one of which carries data no rule authenticates.
candidates.evidence: Model: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANTOURN/seal0.lua builds a height-1 match that diverges at leaf 0 and calls prt.validate_seal_response with agreed_state_hash_proof = { target_address = 12345, log2_target_size = 7, log2_root_size = 3, target_hash = 'junk', root_hash = 'x', sibling_hashes = { 'not', 'a', 'proof' } }; it is accepted (output: 'seal at leaf zero with a junk agreed-state proof accepted: true 0 true'). The same script's k.lua run showed cartesi.fromjson under 'RevealBisectionResponse' accepts missing and unknown fields. Dave: by reading only (Match.sol _requireAgreeState returns before using agreeStateProof when divergencePosition == 0); not executed on the chain harness.
candidates.test_idea: Model: require('prt'), build a match with new_match at height 1 and position 0 whose left leaves differ, call validate_seal_response with a non-nil (junk) agreed_state_hash_proof and assert that it raises; exit 1 while it returns a divergence. Dave: on the local chain with the released contracts, drive a leaf (or root) match to READY_TO_SEAL at runningLeafPosition 0 with left leaves that differ and call sealLeafMatch (or sealInnerMatchAndCreateInnerTournament) with _agreeHash = initialHash and a non-empty _agreeHashProof (for example 1000 random words); assert the call reverts; exit 1 while it succeeds and emits LeafMatchSealed / NewInnerTournament.

candidates.title: Manual misdescribes the released Dave geometry ('the same two levels over a larger epoch') and contradicts its own transcript on who sends the elimination
candidates.component: Manual doc/README.md, section 'Permissionless refereed tournament' (intro and 'Running the tournament'); compared with Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 ArbitrationConstants (released) and doc/recipes/prt.lua new_dapp_contract / game-transport.lua
candidates.role: Manual (the normative referee model of section 5) against the Referee model as deployed (Dave) and the recipe's Referee model
candidates.location: doc/README.md ~10445-10451 ('The demonstration samples the mcycle claim once every 2^10 mcycles (p = 10) ... Dave's ArbitrationConstants.sol uses the same two levels over a larger epoch.'); bugs/harness/work/dave/released/prt/contracts/src/arbitration-config/ArbitrationConstants.sol (log2step [38, 0], height [54, 38]); doc/recipes/prt.lua new_dapp_contract (geometry = new_geometry(10): heights 62 and 30). Second instance: doc/README.md ~11156-11164 ('At the elimination deadline the honest player sends the elimination' followed by the printed line 'An elimination response from tamperer removes both inactive claims.'); doc/recipes/game-transport.lua step_time/accept_scheduled_response (replies ordered by request id, then connection order).
candidates.description: (a) The released Dave constants cover exactly the same epoch as the model and the emulator: height(0) + log2step(0) = 54 + 38 = 92 = 24 + 48 + 20, the model's 62 + 30. What differs is the sampling period of the mcycle claim, 2^18 mcycles in Dave against 2^10 in the model (so the uarch claim has 2^38 leaves instead of 2^30). The manual states the difference as 'a larger epoch', which is false, and its list of simplifications does not name the sampling period, although section 5 makes every unlisted disagreement between the model and a deployed referee 'a defect in one of the two' and R13 counts 'the dispute constants' (the sampling period among them) as part of the protocol. (b) In 'Running the tournament' the prose says the honest player sends the elimination of the quitters' match, while the transcript printed right after it, and the code, credit the tamperer: every live player answers the elimination request and the transport takes the first valid reply in connection order.
candidates.trigger: A reader (operator or deployer) who takes the manual's description of the deployed referee's constants at face value; no adversary action.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: no. 2. Role: the manual's model is normative for the referee (section 5: 'The manual's permissionless refereed tournament is the normative model of what the referee verifies and derives. The simplifications that the manual lists for it are not normative, and neither are its clock values. Any other disagreement between a deployed referee and the model is a defect in one of the two.'). 3. High/Medium cases: none matches; section 8 adds 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' If the manual were right (Dave differing only by a larger epoch), nothing in the behavior would be unsafe; the honest player and bridge read the geometry from the chain (prt-bridge read_geometry) and accept p = 18. 4. Critical: no rule or obligation is violated at a reachable state or on the honest operator's path; R13 ('The dispute constants') is touched only as a documentation mismatch between two deployments, not as versions mixed within one. 5. Low: 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model'. Alternative reading that would raise it: if the model's sampling period is taken as normative for a deployed referee because it is not a listed simplification, the released period 2^18 is an unlisted disagreement; the facts that decide are whether section 5 means the model's constant p or only its two-level structure.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None directly. It leaves the one dispute constant in which the model and the released referee differ (the sampling period, which also drives the uarch-claim build cost that A7 must cover, see R1-A7-1) undocumented and misdescribed.
candidates.evidence: Read ArbitrationConstants.sol (released) and doc/recipes/prt-contracts.patch (which changes [38,0]/[54,38] to [30,0]/[62,30] for the recipe); 54+38 = 62+30 = 92. The manual's transcript line names the tamperer while the sentence before it names the honest player; event_handler.eliminate_match of every shared-code player returns 'nothing' and emit_eliminate_match accepts the first reply.
candidates.test_idea: A documentation check: assert that the manual's sentence about ArbitrationConstants names the sampling period (2^18 mcycles) and the same 2^92 epoch, and that the prose about match 4 names the player the transcript names. No behavioral test.

not_covered: Dave Tournament/Match/Clock/MatchClocks, the factory, CartesiStateTransition, DaveConsensus and the rollups-contracts validity-proof libraries were compared with the manual's model by reading only; nothing was executed on the local chain harness (no forge test, no anvil run). Conclusions reached by reading: the bisection, the seal (parity of the revealer, agreed-state proof), validContestedFinalState, the parent commitment derived from the child winner's final state, the windows [b+c, b+c+w) and elimination from b+c+w, the join deduction, the child allowance max(r1, r2), the leaf-race rule and the counter-to-form map all agree with the manual apart from the listed simplifications and the differences earlier rounds reported (R1-A2-2, R2-DFCLAIM-1).

Dave clock sizing (ClockBudgets, COMMITMENT_BUDGET, refill and envelope) against worst-case costs: only the conservation argument was re-derived (an honest claim that acts within one response budget is never charged, and a child return restores min(carried + refill, envelope)). Whether the budgets cover replaying an input from its boundary to the disputed period or leaf (R12 'Reaching that position costs at most the mcycles from the nearest retained input boundary') depends on the validator node's checkpoints, which are out of scope; not quantified.

The number of sequential matches that Dave's asynchronous pairing lets a Sybil population force on the honest claim (the manual says 'logarithmic in N' for PRT and that Dave builds on it); not analysed beyond noting that the honest clock is not drained by it.
Bonds and refunds (listed simplification 'no bonds change hands').

The game transport (game-transport.lua) was read in full for scheduling (block barrier, prompt and scheduled replies, first-valid ordering, deadlines); no derivation defect found (a prompt honest reply is always included at B+1, late or early replies are refused by the validators' windows, closed futures make later replies stale). Its stall and crash classes (R1-A8-3, R3-VARREFMODEL-1/2) were not re-reported; malformed-message fuzzing was not done.

End-to-end runs of the referee model with the honest forked player were limited to: a zero-input epoch with a scratch adversary lying at mcycle leaves 0, 1, 2^38-1, 2^38, (2^24-1)*2^38 and 2^62-1 (uarch leaf 0, ordinary step in an empty slot); an epoch whose input 0 is rejected by the calculator (payload 'a=1'), disputing the rejecting period at its last uarch leaf (prt-dishonest fabulist used as a tool), at the reset that closes the rejecting instruction (uarch leaf 541*2^20-1, leads to the revert hash) and at the first step after it (from the canonical state); and the delivery of the next input after that rejection. All settled on the honest claim. Not run: the eight-player demonstration and its printed hashes, timeouts and eliminations with real players, halting or exception-yielding guests, inputs larger than the rx buffer, stored-mode players, sampling periods other than 2^10.

The printed transcripts and hashes of 'Running the tournament' (claims, uarch claims, final hash, the proved output) were not regenerated; only their internal consistency was read (leaf indices, heights, forms of transition).

The player-side statements of 'Computation hashes with repetition' and 'The player' (bundle counts 'about nine thousand', 'the mcycle forest already holds that leaf's path', forest authentication of opened bundles, stored mode and reflinks) were checked by reading prt.lua and cartesi.hash-tree.lua (frontier_forest_expand_leaf asserts the bundle root before installing), not measured.

prt-lua-bridge.md, crisium.lua, prt-bridge.lua and the chain bridge (outside this slice of doc/README.md); the dishonest strategies and the test harnesses (out of scope; prt-dishonest.lua was only run as a tool).
